prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” interior painter for every homeowner — the right company depends on your budget, the size and condition of the job, the quality level you want, timetable, and how you like to work with contractors. I can, however, help you find the best option for you. Two quick paths:

- If you want a recommendation now: tell me your zip code or neighborhood and any preferences (budget vs. high-end finish, need for color consultation, timeline). I can then narrow things down and tell you what to look for in each local candidate.
- If you’d rather evaluate companies yourself, use the checklist below to identify the best contractor for your job.

Checklist to find the best interior painting company
1. Verify credentials
  - Licensed (if required locally), insured (general liability and workers’ comp).
  - Bonded if requested.
  - Check BBB rating and recent Google/Yelp reviews; read several recent reviews, not just the star rating.

2. Ask for examples and references
  - Photos of recent jobs like yours (same room type, ceiling height, trim detail).
  - At least 2–3 references you can call.

3. Get detailed written bids (compare at least 3)
  - Scope of work: surfaces to be painted, prep (patching, sanding, caulking), number of coats, primers.
  - Materials: brand and sheen of paint, low-VOC options.
  - Timeline and cleanup plan.
  - Price breakdown (labor vs. materials).
  - Payment schedule and written warranty on workmanship.

4. Evaluate surface prep and quality controls
  - Proper surface prep is the biggest determinant of a long-lasting finish.
  - Ask if they back-roll/brush trim, use sprayers, or use both (sprayer + back-brushing is standard for a high-quality finish).

5. Confirm scheduling and communication
  - Who will be your point of contact? Will the crew be the same each day?
  - How will unexpected issues (rot, drywall repairs) be handled and priced?

6. Look for extras that show professionalism
  - Color consultation, sample/test patches on walls, protection of floors and furniture, daily cleanup, final walk-through.

Typical cost benchmarks (St. Louis region, 2023–2024 ranges)
  - Per square foot interior painting: roughly $1.50–$4.00/ft² depending on prep and paint quality.
  - Per room (average bedroom): $300–800 for two coats, depending on size and trim work.
  - Trim-only or high-detail rooms can be more expensive.

If you want, give me:
  - Your zip code,
  - Type of job (single room, whole house, high ceilings, trim-only),
  - Any companies you’ve already considered,
and I’ll help shortlist local painters and give tailored questions to ask each.
